Table III shows the final module and system costs along with calculated LCOE values for Kanas City MO, USA. Comparing similar efficiency cells (module efficiencies were derated by one absolute precent from cell values) made from the Siemens + Cz wafers (column 1) to the baseline Fz-CVD wafers (column 2), several differences in the inputs standout. The Fz-CVD process has: 1) a lower wafer/hour/tool and a larger number of tools due to the lower effective growth rate 2) lower tool downtime and consumables due to an overall simpler process 3) twice the cost for a Fz-CVD puller, compared to a Cz puller, due to the lack of a commercial product, but likely similar to a slightly modified Fz puller produced at scale 4) less workforce needed to run a fully automated Fz-CVD puller compared to running both the Siemens process and Cz pullers 5) higher cell costs due to the increased price of the wafer. The degradation rate and service life were set to that of a proxy Longi HI-MO7 TOPCon module [14]. The results of the baseline case are that the cost to produce 24% TOPCon cells from Fz-CVD wafers is about 3.3x higher ($/W) compared to traditionally grown cells (Table II). This translates to 1.8x higher module prices, 1.24x installed system costs, and 1.17x higher LCOE. So, for making incumbent cells from the Fz-CVD wafers there is only an energy and CO saving, but no 2 economic driver. However, the key advantage of the Fz-CVD wafers is their potentially high lifetimes and low impurities which allow champion efficiencies and state-of-the-art low degradation rates and long service lifetimes. To capture these benefits in our modeling we ran two scenarios that gave 28% efficient cells [15]; one with Fz-CVD wafers produced at 120 µm/min deposition rate and one at 300 µm/min to represent a stretch goal for the technology. Table III, column 3 shows the results for the 120 µm/min deposition rate with similar inputs as the baseline case (column 2). However, the cells costs are higher to account for the added steps needed to make a higher efficiency cell (e.g. advanced TOPCon) [16] and the degradation rate is set to that of a Maxeon module with a record low degradation rate of 0.25%/year [17]. The service life in columns 3 and 4 is extended to match the end-of-life percent power loss of the Longi module (87.4%) to make a direct comparison between columns.
